english: Let $A=\{1,2,3,\dots,40\}$ and let $R$ be the relation on $A$ defined by $(a,b)\in R$ if and only if $b$ is the largest odd divisor of $a$. Let $R^{-1}$ denote the inverse of $R$, and let $S$ be the relation on $A$ consisting of all ordered pairs $(a,c)\in A\times A$ for which there exists $b\in A$ with $(a,b)\in R$ and $(b,c)\in R^{-1}$. Then the number of elements in $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना $A=\{1,2,3,\dots,40\}$ है तथा $A$ पर संबंध $R$ इस प्रकार परिभाषित है कि $(a,b)\in R$ यदि और केवल यदि $b$, $a$ का सबसे बड़ा विषम भाजक है। माना $R^{-1}$, $R$ का प्रतिलोम संबंध है तथा $S$, $A$ पर वह संबंध है जिसमें वे सभी क्रमित युग्म $(a,c)\in A\times A$ हैं जिनके लिए कोई $b\in A$ ऐसा है कि $(a,b)\in R$ तथा $(b,c)\in R^{-1}$ है। तब $S$ में अवयवों की संख्या ______ है।
solution: Let $o(a)$ = largest odd divisor of $a$; $(a,b)\in R\iff b=o(a)$
$(b,c)\in R^{-1}\iff(c,b)\in R\iff b=o(c)$, so $(a,c)\in S\iff o(a)=o(c)$
$S$ is an equivalence relation; classes $\{m,2m,4m,\dots\}\cap A$, $m$ odd
solution_full: For $a\in A$ write $a=2^{r}m$ with $m$ odd; then $m=o(a)$ is the largest odd divisor of $a$ and $o(a)\le a\le40$, so $o(a)\in A$. Thus $(a,b)\in R\iff b=o(a)$, and each $a$ has exactly one image.
By definition of the inverse, $(b,c)\in R^{-1}\iff(c,b)\in R\iff b=o(c)$.
So $(a,c)\in S$ iff some $b\in A$ satisfies $b=o(a)$ and $b=o(c)$, i.e. iff $o(a)=o(c)$.

"Having the same largest odd divisor" is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, so $S$ is an equivalence relation on $A$. The class of an odd $m$ is $\{m,2m,4m,\dots\}\cap A$, and a class with $s$ elements contributes $s^{2}$ ordered pairs.
originality_note: New: composing the 'largest odd divisor' relation with its inverse to produce the 'same odd part' equivalence relation and counting its pairs by class sizes (way 5: composition and inverse of relations linked with equivalence classes). Closest known: 'R o R^{-1} for a given finite relation' textbook exercises and the 'chains m, 2m, 4m' idea from divisibility selection problems. Different because: the composition has to be decoded into an equivalence relation before the classes can be counted.

concept_use.Composition and inverse of relations: S is the composite of R followed by R^{-1}; decoding it with (b,c) in R^{-1} iff (c,b) in R gives o(a) = o(c).
concept_use.Equivalence relations and equivalence cl: S is the 'same largest odd divisor' equivalence relation; its classes {m,2m,4m,...} give n(S) as a sum of squares of class sizes.
